_note: Single source for every number displayed on the GeoAFT pages and figures. Values are copied verbatim from the cited sources; do not round them here. Comparator R positions on the recovery figure are derived from the reported margins, not measured directly. Update this file (and rerun build_figures.py) when per-target values are released.

sources.proposal: GeoAFT preliminary evidence as summarised in the author's research proposal (v11, October 2026), Prior Work section

metric.name: oracle-gap recovery
metric.definition: R = (L_base - L_method) / (L_base - L_oracle), where L is the KL divergence from the target attention distribution on held-out synthetic data. R = 1 means the method closes the whole gap the target-generating oracle closes; R = 0 means no improvement over the unadapted base. It is not classification accuracy.

controlled_targets.setting: synthetic, fixed representations, known target compatibility function
controlled_targets.pair_mlp_paired_cells: positive in all 25 paired cells on each target
controlled_targets.margin_scope: range across the two targets; the per-target assignment of each end of the range is not reproduced here
qualifiers: The fixed L_p geometry bank nearly exhausted the available oracle gap on the L_p target, so the L_p superiority gate could not be met.
The exact quadratic (bilinear-plus-key-quadratic) control outperformed the Mahalanobis overlay, as the analytic equivalence predicts.

nonlinear_target.qualifier: The recovery advantage is below the preregistered materiality threshold; the result supports economy, not superiority. Parameter counts are trainable parameters, not inference cost.

analytic.mahalanobis_equivalence: -(q-k)^T M (q-k) = 2 q^T M k - k^T M k - q^T M q; the last term is constant across keys and cancels under row-wise softmax, so squared-Mahalanobis compatibility is softmax-equivalent to a bilinear-plus-key-quadratic score.

not_claimed: broad or current state of the art
new Mahalanobis expressivity beyond the equivalent score family
